text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Vassily Melnik has been chosen for the post of finance minister following consultations between the Democratic Party Saimnieks and Prime Minister Andris Shkele. Shkele said he was convinced that the new minister will be approved by the parliament on Thursday.

- Director of Latvijas Pasts offered his resignation after an armed robbery on a post courier vehicle which left three post employees dead last Saturday. Some 135,800 lats was stolen. The transport minister rejected the resignation offer.
- Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjorn Tore Godal arrived in Riga on an official visit to discuss security issues and the abolition of visa requirements in travel between the two countries.

- The board of Latvia's Way party approved the list of candidates for local elections in Riga. The list is headed by Employment Minister Andris Berzinsh, former higher education minister Janis Gaigals and Romualdas Razukas, former leader of the Latvian Popular Front.

- The government passed three draft laws under article 81 of the Constitution, which means it can pass legislation prior to parliament approval. The laws included amendments to the law on privatisation.
- Shkele and nationalist party Fatherland & Freedom reached a compromise on the certification of slaughter-houses, which will now take effect in summer this year instead of January 1.
- State-owned Latvian Railways announced a tender for the modernisation of Riga railway station. The company to win the competition will be offered a lease on the station building.
- Russia's new ambassador to Latvia, Alexander Udaltsov, is due to arrive in Riga next week, the press office of the Latvian foreign ministry announced.
- British Airways received a licence for regular flights to Riga.
